banned: Do not ship until the origin Competent Authority confirms whether the Ban Amendment or national law prohibits the movement
Confirm whether the material is hazardous waste (A1181 for hazardous e-waste; Y49 for other e-waste)
Confirm the origin State's current Ban Amendment status and national export restrictions
If prohibited, use a lawful alternative route/destination or do not proceed
high: Obtain waste characterization and hazardous constituent analysis
Apply to your national Competent Authority for notification approval
Submit formal PIC request to destination CA and await written consent
Arrange transit country consents if routing through non-Basel-party states
Complete Basel notification document with all supporting documentation
Ensure carrier is licensed for transboundary hazardous waste movement
Retain all consent letters — movement documents must accompany waste
medium: Confirm waste classification — verify Basel code and hazard status
Notify your national Competent Authority of intended transboundary movement
Obtain Prior Informed Consent from destination CA (written)
Prepare Basel notification document and movement documents
Ensure financial guarantee is in place before shipment
Carrier must hold appropriate transboundary waste transport authorization
low: Document the waste/non-waste determination and evidence of functionality where used equipment is claimed as non-waste
Check current national controls in export, import and every transit State
For e-waste that is waste, verify A1181/Y49 control requirements before shipment
Retain competent-authority confirmations and movement documentation required for the route

transitWarnings.Caribbean-to-Europe: Identify every planned State of transit. Under Basel Article 6(4), prior written transit consent is required unless that Party has waived it; national definitions and maritime practices can differ, so confirm the route with each relevant Competent Authority.
